meta.purpose: The decision logic, captured. Not styling — the rules that decide styling, tiered and sourced. Nothing here is invented: every rule cites Style Guide v1.4 or a Decision Book rule ID.
meta.source: Nightlife Culture Style Guide v1.4 + The Decision Book (digest 6034d466ccbf4071)

tiers.fixed: There is a right answer. Pass or fail, measurable. Breaking it is negligence.
tiers.adaptable: No single correct answer. Defensible or not. Choosing is the job.
tiers.decorative: Free — provided nothing carrying meaning lives there.

meta.sourceRead: All 18 chapters of The Decision Book read in full, 16 August 2026 — not the CSV registers. 4,596 lines.
meta.correction: An earlier pass reported that 'provenance chip' and 'callout' have no basis in the Book's prose. That was wrong for the chip: ch04 specifies the self-describing chip and the ordinal strength meter explicitly, as named patterns with rules. Carly's .nc-prov and .nc-meter come straight from it. 'Callout' remains absent.

rules.rule: Every accent takes ink text. Every ground takes the text colour its own token declares: white on blue and ink, ink on chalk and white. Read the ground off tokens.json — never off a remembered sentence.
rules.breaks: The old wording — 'every ground is a white-text surface' — is false for two of the four grounds. White on chalk is 1.1096:1 and white on white is 1.0000:1. An agent that followed it literally shipped an invisible surface believing it had complied, and the sentence carrying the defect was the one flagged 'if you remember nothing else, remember that'.
rules.machine: no light-ground class sets a white or near-white text colour

rules.rule: Only the four-series ramp encodes data. Brand accents are surfaces.
rules.breaks: Accents separate by hue alone and collapse in greyscale.

rules.rule: Four series maximum. One series = blue.
rules.breaks: Beyond four the ramp stops being distinguishable.

rules.rule: Label at the mark. Decide labelling before series colour.
rules.breaks: For brand-derived palettes, direct labelling is the mechanism by which the chart is compliant at all.

rules.rule: Retired colours are never reintroduced: #920DFF #F26B43 #FFD100 #F6F6EE. Aptos is a retired typeface.
rules.breaks: Reintroduction is silent drift.

rules.rule: No colour value may appear in an artefact that is not in tokens.json.
rules.breaks: A hand-picked hex is a decision made outside the system, and it will be made differently next time.

rules.rule: Blue is a structural signal, not scattered decoration.
rules.breaks: Scattered accent reads as decoration and stops signalling.

rules.rule: Caps are applied as a character format (text-transform / All Caps), never typed.
rules.breaks: Typed caps are read letter-by-letter by screen readers and cannot be undone.

rules.rule: Body 12pt floor. Line height 1.5–1.6 running prose, 1.25–1.35 table cells.
rules.breaks: Below the floor the document stops being readable at distance or in print.

rules.rule: Body and H3 are sentence case. Never caps in body, captions, source lines or table cells.
rules.breaks: Caps below ~16pt stop working.

rules.rule: Caps floor is 16pt. Resolves the §08 conflict between the 14pt label minimum and the H3 note.
rules.breaks: Unresolved, the next person picks a different number.

rules.rule: Fonts embedded in every deliverable. Never linked.
rules.breaks: Substitution widens the same string by roughly a third, silently.

rules.source: v1.4 §09 · containment v1.3 (which retracts grounds v1.2's 'structural hairline')
rules.rule: Contain with colour and space, not outlines. The 2px ink outline is reserved for the flyer register — covers, posters, section dividers — never the default.
rules.breaks: Used full-time it does the work space should do and makes every panel shout at the same volume. Reserved, the box means something when it turns up.

rules.rule: Hairline is never used for anything carrying meaning. White panels on chalk, tables and forms only.
rules.breaks: A meaning-carrying container held by a hairline is invisible in print and to a screen reader.

rules.rule: Pull quotes, callouts and asides use the left rule (12px). Dense pages and tables use the top rule (9px). Accent panels use fill.
rules.breaks: Treatment carries the register; swapping them flattens the hierarchy.

rules.source: v1.4 §10 · measured in the working deck
rules.rule: Slide side margin 5.25%, kicker line 6.67%. The written 6% / 7.5% is superseded by what the deck does.
rules.breaks: Two grids in one system.

rules.rule: One idea per slide. Roughly half the canvas empty; over ~55% covered means two slides. Remove copy before reducing type.
rules.breaks: Reducing type to fit is how the floor gets broken.

rules.rule: Keep core information in a simple reading order. Single-column for long-form where practical.
rules.breaks: Reading order is invisible on screen and decisive for everyone not looking at it.

rules.rule: Slide grammar: kicker → statement → provocation → structure → so-what. Structure elements are always marker + qualifier, never a marker alone.
rules.breaks: A caps marker without its qualifier is a slogan.
rules.status: PROVISIONAL — pattern read from four slides, awaiting confirmation

rules.rule: Reading order set explicitly, on every slide. Placeholders authored in reading order in the master.
rules.breaks: Reading order follows shape-creation order and bears no relation to visual position.

rules.rule: Every slide carries a unique descriptive title. It may be hidden or off-canvas; it may not be absent.
rules.breaks: It is how a screen-reader user navigates a deck, and the title list is the deck outline.

rules.rule: No tables on slides. A table on a slide is a reference table in the wrong artefact.
rules.breaks: Puts reference density into a presented artefact.

rules.rule: No text box sized to its text.
rules.breaks: A substituted face widens the same string by roughly a third.

rules.rule: Real named styles, applied. Never direct character formatting.
rules.breaks: 100% direct formatting makes the style system inert — measured in both UKDF documents.

rules.rule: A4 for UK submissions.
rules.breaks: Both UKDF documents are US Letter.

rules.rule: Document title, author and one declared language set in properties.
rules.breaks: Neither UKDF document sets a title.

rules.rule: Table header rows repeat across pages.
rules.breaks: Measured: 9 of 57 tables in the funding deck copy.

rules.rule: Headings state findings, not topics. No skipped heading levels. Conclusion in the first screen.
rules.breaks: A contents list of finding-headings is a readable summary, which is what most readers use it as.

rules.rule: White ground for Word and print, not chalk.
rules.breaks: Word and print handle white more predictably, and partners will edit it.

rules.rule: Spreadsheets are models: real tables, formulas from one assumptions sheet, freeze panes, no merged cells in data.
rules.breaks: Measured: 53 formulas in 1,135 cells, 0 tables, 0 freeze panes, 56 merged ranges.

rules.rule: Every chart carries provenance: code, reference period, geography, boundary vintage. Every big number carries a source line.
rules.breaks: A statistic without a source line is a claim, not a finding.

rules.rule: Show the gaps. Hatched for suppressed [c], dashed for a break in collection, n/a for not collected. Never a silent blank.
rules.breaks: A gap in the data is a finding.

rules.rule: No published figure rests on fewer than three contributing units. Apply secondary suppression.
rules.breaks: A value recoverable by subtraction is not suppressed.

rules.rule: Illustrative or placeholder figures say so, in the chart, every time.
rules.breaks: A placeholder that travels becomes a claim.

rules.rule: Every derived artefact states the source version it was built from.
rules.breaks: A wrong stamp is worse than none — an absent stamp prompts a check, a wrong one prevents it.

rules.rule: The wordmark is an outlined asset. Never re-set as live type.
rules.breaks: The two lines are set at different sizes (32.09pt / 33.41pt) so they justify to one width. One size loses the lockup.

rules.rule: Minimalist. Bright colour, breathing space, message carries. No icons, illustration, stickers or decorative imagery.
rules.breaks: Nothing — this is the decorative tier. The joy comes from what the work is doing, not from ornament.

rules.rule: A section header must BE a heading, not look like one. The numeral box sits inside the heading element.
rules.breaks: Found in headers.html: .nc-section-head is a div of spans. It renders as the document's H2 level and contains no heading — the exact 'appearance and structure are independent' failure, inside the component that structures every document.

rules.rule: Apply the suppression threshold to the planned sample BEFORE fieldwork is scoped, and state at proposal stage what the design will let you say.
rules.breaks: Measured in the Book against a budget model of this exact shape: two places, 18-24 conversations, gives 9-12 per place. A threshold of three survives a single frequency count and nothing else — every place x role, place x age cross-tabulation falls below it. The comparative claim the research exists to make is the claim disclosure will not let you publish. It looks like a budget line, taken months before anyone opens a chart library.

rules.rule: One source per number, named, wherever a figure appears in more than one artefact. Reconcile across the pack before submission, as a step.
rules.breaks: Measured in a four-artefact funding pack: workbook said £50,000, application draft and deck both said £49,800, no mapping. One assumptions cell labelled 'UKDF request' with a basis column reading 'Application ceiling'. A fund manager finds it in thirty seconds and it reads as not knowing what you are asking for.

rules.rule: Where artefacts disagree, date them and name the most recent as the candidate truth. Never report an unresolved contradiction and hand the job back.
rules.breaks: A contradiction reported without a candidate answer transfers the whole job to the author at 11pm.

rules.rule: State where the current version lives, in the system itself. Name the canonical location once; treat every other copy as derived.
rules.breaks: Versioning without a location leaves a reviewer several candidates — a repo folder, a project, a chat, a skill — and no way to choose.

rules.rule: Quote the line every finding rests on, or mark the finding as inference. Report an absence as a different class of claim from a quotation.
rules.breaks: Findings drift from 'the document says' to 'you said' in three cheap steps. Measured during the Book's own review — and committed again in this project when an absence was reported for the provenance chip, which ch04 specifies explicitly.

rules.rule: Do not build a generic diagram kit of nodes and connectors. Name the job — bound, relate, decompose, sequence, diverge, converge — and use a named form from the vocabulary, stating which it is.
rules.breaks: A generic kit produces the default flowchart, which asserts sequence when the job is boundary or influence. Every arrow is a claim about order or causation. Closes v1.4 §15 gap 2 differently than the guide anticipated.

rules.rule: A keyline on a chart mark is exempt from the hard-outline rule. Where marks touch or overlap, ch04 requires 3:1 adjacency OR a separator, border or pattern — the keyline IS that mechanism.
rules.breaks: Without it the dot-plot point disappears into its own range bar. This is a graphic doing separation work, not a container drawn around content. Named so the exemption is visible rather than silent.

rules.rule: Every spatial value — padding, margin, gap — comes from the spacing scale. One base unit (.25em), nine steps, non-linear. Rule weights are not spacing and are exempt.
rules.breaks: Measured in this repo: the page scaffold used twenty distinct ad-hoc pixel values and the component layer had 51 spacing declarations off any scale. One unit produces relationships a reader can learn; none produces noise that reads as carelessness. joy.css already carried a measured scale, defined and never used.

rules.rule: Logo colour is not governed by text contrast. WCAG 1.4.3 exempts text that is part of a logo or brand name, and ch04 carries that Essential exception naming logos. Any accent may be used for the wordmark on any ground, chosen for the register — the wordmark's weight, not a contrast ratio, is what carries it.
rules.breaks: Furniture v1.6 barred teal on a light ground on a 1.52:1 reading. That applied a body-text threshold to a logotype, which the standard exempts and which the display weight makes moot in practice. The reading was wrong, not the logo. Recorded so it cannot be re-raised: this has now been raised and withdrawn twice.
rules.supersedes: furniture v1.6 §03 — 'teal is never a logo colour on a light ground'

rules.rule: One component layer, sized in em. The context sets the base and the component scales itself against it — .nc-doc for documents, .nc-slide .cv for slides. Never hard-code px inside a component; never redefine a component inside a context file.
rules.breaks: Two component sets that look alike and drift apart. A pull quote in a report and a pull quote on a slide stop being the same thing, and every fix has to be made twice. This is what the handover diagnosed: the system drifted because it was built from the slides outwards rather than from the rule set outwards.
rules.machine: no px length inside a component block; context files set font-size and nothing else

rules.rule: Colour is a modifier, never baked into a component. A component declares var(--nc-acc) with a default; an accent class supplies the value.
rules.breaks: A component per colour. Six pull quotes instead of one with six modifiers, and the seventh accent means a seventh component.
rules.machine: component blocks reference --nc-acc, not a named colour token

rules.rule: The breakout stat has three variants and they are chosen by context, not taste. Left rule is the default, in running text. Top rule where stats sit in a row or on a table-heavy page, so five filled panels do not shout at once. Filled where one number is the whole point — slides and covers. The source line is part of the component in all three.
rules.breaks: Filled stats used as the default, which turns a page of evidence into a paint chart and leaves the reader no way to tell which number is the finding.

rules.source: ch06 step seven · joy.html §03 · charts v1.4 §06
rules.rule: A statistic without its reference period, geography and provenance is a claim, not a finding. The source line is not optional and is not a caption — it belongs to the stat.
rules.breaks: A number that cannot be checked, reused or challenged. The evidence standard separates a finding from a claim; a stat with no source line collapses the distinction.

rules.rule: A breaker is a pause, not an ornament. One per surface. Two rules stop meaning 'pause' and start meaning 'pattern'.
rules.breaks: Rules read as decoration, so the reader stops using them to find the shape of the argument.
rules.machine: at most one .nc-brk per slide or section

rules.rule: The separator sits between the title zone and the body zone, flush to the left margin, 20% wide. Blue on light grounds, teal on dark. It is a paragraph break for a surface — never inside a statement.
rules.breaks: A rule in the middle of a sentence interrupts it rather than pacing it. Retired for exactly that reason.

rules.source: furniture v1.6 §02 · slide layouts v1.0 L5 · v1.4 §10
rules.rule: The accent bar sits ABOVE a pull quote and nowhere else. It is the only decorative use of a breaker, and it is always at the top.
rules.breaks: Decoration that migrates. Once the bar can appear anywhere it stops signalling a quote and becomes a texture.

rules.rule: The hairline breaker is the quieter alternative — full measure, under a title, on dense or document-register surfaces. The short accent separator is the deck register; the hairline is the report register. They may coexist across formats, not on one surface.
rules.breaks: Two pacing systems on one page, so neither reads as deliberate.

rules.source: charts v1.4 §03 · v1.4 §12 · Comparative Place-Based Research Methodology v1.0
rules.rule: Any chart comparing two or more places carries a comparability note stating whether the indicator gate has been cleared, and which of concept, unit, reference period, geography basis, boundary vintage, population, classification and method required harmonising. A comparison without it is not publishable.
rules.breaks: Two numbers presented as one series when they measure different things. The design does the overstating, silently, because a shared axis asserts comparability whether or not it holds.
rules.machine: a chart with two or more place categories contains .nc-comp

rules.rule: Illustrative or placeholder figures carry the flag inside the chart, on the marks, every time. Not in a footnote, not in the covering note.
rules.breaks: Charts travel. The moment one is screenshotted into a board paper the footnote is gone and the placeholder reads as a measurement.

rules.rule: Show the gaps as gaps. Hatched fill for a value suppressed for disclosure control [c]; the marker n/a where the value was not collected for this population; a dashed segment for a break in collection. The row always stays.
rules.breaks: A dropped row hides a finding. A silent blank asserts nothing was there. Both are stronger claims than the data supports, and both are invisible to the reader.
rules.machine: no blank value cells in a chart component

rules.rule: Gridlines sit at 10% ink. Present enough to read against, quiet enough to disappear, and never heavier than the data.
rules.breaks: Grid competing with marks. The reader's eye is pulled to the scaffolding rather than the shape of the finding.
rules.machine: --nc-grid is the only stroke used for gridlines

rules.rule: Change over time is a line, with series labelled at the line and never in a legend. A break in collection is drawn as a dashed segment and never interpolated across.
rules.breaks: Interpolating a break is a design decision masquerading as data — it draws a trend nobody measured. A legend makes the reader hold a colour key while reading the shape.
rules.machine: .nc-line uses .ln--break for collection breaks; no legend element

rules.rule: Modelled or surveyed values are drawn with their interval. A range bar where uncertainty is material; a dot plot with its range where places are compared on an indicator.
rules.breaks: A bare point estimate reads as a count. A bar with no visible range makes a model look like a measurement — the single most common way a chart overstates its evidence.

rules.source: charts v1.4 §04 · v1.4 §12 chart types · grounds v1.2
rules.rule: Parts of a whole: the donut is the default, the 100% stacked bar wherever two or more wholes are compared, and the pie is permitted when one dominant share must be instantly recognisable. Four segments maximum in all three, percentages always in the key, and a keyline between touching segments.
rules.breaks: Two pies side by side, which is the hardest comparison in the whole vocabulary. Past four slices none of the three is readable by anyone.

rules.rule: No non-uniform scaling. A chart or image is never stretched to fit — the container flexes, the coordinate space does not.
rules.breaks: Stretching survives in the lines and destroys the type. It looks like a rendering fault to everyone except the person who made it.

rules.rule: Alt text states the finding, not the chart type. Anything load-bearing also ships a data alternative — a real table or a downloadable file — and the chart travels as a vector, never a bare image.
rules.breaks: “Line chart of venue counts” tells a screen-reader user the shape of the file and nothing about the argument. A chart that is only an image cannot be checked, reused or read aloud.
rules.machine: every <figure class=nc-chart> has a title in live text and a figcaption

rules.rule: A figure is a package: the mark, a caption that is not the title, and the source. The caption qualifies; it never carries the finding.
rules.breaks: A caption doing the title's job, which puts the message where the contents list and the screen reader cannot reach it.

rules.rule: Never band and rule at once. A table groups its rows with zoning bands or with rules, not both.
rules.breaks: Two grouping mechanisms doing one job, so neither reads as deliberate and the eye has to decide which to trust.
rules.machine: a .nc-table--band row carries no bottom border

rules.rule: Editorial is the default table and the only one that needs no class. The accent table marks a table that belongs to the section above it; the banded table is for long reference tables where the eye needs a rail. Numbers are right-aligned with tabular figures in all three.
rules.breaks: A table style chosen by eye, so two tables in one document group their rows differently and the reader infers a distinction that is not there.

rules.source: furniture v1.6 §02 · slide layouts v1.0 L2 · v1.4 §10
rules.rule: The stop sits under a divider title with nothing after it. Teal on dark grounds. Nothing following the rule is the whole point of it.
rules.breaks: A divider that carries content stops being a divider. The rule then reads as a separator promising more, and the pause is lost.

rules.rule: Remove copy before reducing type. Type size is a floor, not a variable — when content does not fit, the content is too long.
rules.breaks: Reducing type to fit is how the floor gets broken, and it breaks it invisibly: the slide looks finished and is unreadable from four rows back. This is the rule that protects all the other typographic rules.

rules.rule: Build from the rule set outwards, never from the slides outwards. Slides are one application of the component layer, alongside documents, charts, web pages and marcoms. A new need adds a rule and a component, not a one-off slide.
rules.breaks: The diagnosis from the last rebuild: a system built from the slides outwards has no document layer, so every report is authored by hand and every hand-authored value is a fork.

rules.rule: Render the decision rather than describing it. A design decision arrives as something to look at, or it waits. Sheets that explain the system are generated from the system, so they cannot describe behaviour it does not have.
rules.breaks: Described decisions cannot be judged. They get agreed in prose and disagreed in artwork, and the disagreement surfaces at the deadline.
rules.machine: every explanatory page is produced by a generator in the build

rules.source: decision sheet · ch03 step eight · v1.4 §14
rules.rule: Every element the browser will render is decided: specified, inherits, or barred. Unstyled is still a look, and it is the one nobody chose.
rules.breaks: Default user-agent styling appearing inside a branded page — a Times serif blockquote, a 1.5rem h4, a blue underlined link — which reads as an error rather than a choice.

rules.rule: Highlight, emphasis and status never rest on colour alone. A mark carries weight as well as fill; an abbreviation is written out in full on first use; a defined term keeps its definition in the prose, not only in a tooltip.
rules.breaks: Meaning that disappears in greyscale, on a projector, or for a screen-reader user — the meaning layer is exactly where accessibility takes the veto.

rules.rule: Progressive disclosure never hides anything load-bearing. A details block holds detail; the finding stays in the open.
rules.breaks: A finding behind a twisty is a finding most readers never meet, and one no printed copy contains at all.

rules.rule: Small text is secondary, never a way to get under the floor. The 12pt body floor and the 13px note floor apply to it as they apply to everything else.
rules.breaks: Source lines, captions and footnotes shrinking until the evidence layer is the least readable thing on the page.
rules.machine: no font-size below the floor on .nc-small, .nc-caption, .nc-source

rules.rule: Every interactive element has a visible focus state, and the focus ring is exempt from the hard-outline rule. Containment v1.3 names focus states as one of the four places the 3:1 non-text threshold genuinely applies — the ring IS that mechanism.
rules.breaks: A keyboard user with no idea where they are. Quietening the ring to match the house containment style trades a required signal for a stylistic preference, which is the wrong way round the decision stack.
rules.machine: a :focus-visible outline of at least 2px on every interactive element

rules.source: tokens.json space.slide · furniture v1.6 §05 · v1.4 §10 · measured in the working deck
rules.rule: The slide top margin is set by what leads the slide: 4% where a kicker leads, 6.667% where a title leads, 13.333% where a full-bleed element leads. Side margins 5.25%. All are multiples of one unit, 1.3333% of slide height.
rules.breaks: One flat top margin gives a statement the kicker's margin, so the slide top-loads and loses the air the statement needs to land. The variation is the mechanism that tells the reader what is leading.
rules.machine: slide top margin is one of the three declared steps

rules.rule: The bottom 13.333% is reserved on every slide — covers and closing slides included. Content never enters it.
rules.breaks: In a room the bottom of the screen is the hardest place to read: heads sit in the sightline. The reserve is about legibility, not about whether a number is printed there, so it does not vary by slide type. Two grids would mean the cover is the one slide whose foot is unreadable.
rules.machine: no content below 86.667% of slide height

rules.rule: Every content area declares where it pins — bottom, centre, split or top. Implicit top-anchoring is barred.
rules.breaks: A dead band across the bottom third. This was the single largest cause of weak slides in the earlier system, and it is invisible until the slide is beside another one.
rules.machine: every .nc-pad carries data-anchor or takes the declared default

rules.rule: Slide numbers are two-digit, bottom right, on content slides only — never a cover or a closing slide. Numbered by position in the deck, not by section.
rules.breaks: People cite slides. Without a number they describe the slide instead, and the description is usually wrong. Position in a sequence is orientation, and it should not exist only in the scrollbar.

rules.rule: The footer wordmark is mono, one colour taken from the ground, roughly 1.5% of slide width — the quietest thing on the slide. The full lockup appears on covers, section dividers and the closing slide only, and the two-colour lockup only there.
rules.breaks: A logo set at heading weight reads as content rather than as a mark. Policy decks get screenshotted and forwarded, so a slide travelling alone should still say who made it — quietly.

rules.rule: Choose the layout from the job: an argument opening takes the divider, three related points the columns, two things in tension the two-column contrast, one line the quote, one number the vertical-third stat, a sequence the ink strip, data the chart slide, detail the vertical third.
rules.breaks: A layout chosen by picture rather than by job, which is how a deck ends up with five arrangements doing the same thing and none of them saying anything.

rules.rule: A layout arranges components; it never defines one. If a layout needs something new, the component layer is missing it — add it there, not in the layout.
rules.breaks: Components born inside slides. That is exactly how the system drifted the first time: twelve layouts each carrying a slightly different pull quote, none of which a document could use.
rules.machine: layout files contain no component definitions

rules.rule: Embed the faces, AND declare a metric-corrected fallback. size-adjust to equalise x-height, ascent-override and descent-override against the adjusted em, line-gap-override to zero.
rules.breaks: Embedding answers 'the font is missing'. It does not answer 'the font has not arrived yet', or the machines that cannot embed at all — email, some PowerPoint installs. Arial at its own metrics is a different size and a different leading, so the page reflows when the real face lands, and every measured layout rule in the system is false for as long as the stand-in is showing.
rules.machine: fonts.css declares size-adjust, ascent-override and descent-override for every fallback

rules.source: Carly, 16 Aug 2026 · v1.4 §07 · closes design-system gap 6
rules.rule: A masthead takes the primary brand colour. Blue. There is one masthead and one measure — no variants, because an unused variant is an invitation to pick by eye.
rules.breaks: Five sheets were built with five hand-written stylesheets and the masthead ground was picked by eye — three ink, two blue. The failure was not the colour. It was that no rule existed, and an answer was invented five separate times rather than the absence being reported.
rules.machine: .nc-mast background is the primary unless .nc-mast--night is declared

rules.rule: Page furniture is a component. Masthead, measure, kicker, standfirst, note and specimen frame are generated from the tokens like everything else. A sheet never carries its own stylesheet.
rules.breaks: A hand-authored page is a fork. The system had ninety components and nothing for the page around them, so every sheet reinvented the frame — and every visual defect found in review lived in that frame rather than in the components.
rules.machine: no per-sheet stylesheet exists; every sheet links foundations/ only

rules.rule: A specimen frame is inert: a hairline and nothing else. Where a specimen carries its own ground, the ground goes on an inner element so the frame cannot override it.
rules.breaks: A frame with an opinion is read as part of the specimen. A dark-ground component demonstrated inside a white frame rendered white, because the frame won on source order — the specimen showed the opposite of what it claimed.

rules.rule: Every interactive element declares its states — visited, hover, focus. A visited link is violet on light grounds and pink on dark.
rules.breaks: A clicked link that looks unclicked, which is the one job link colour has always had. Focus without a ring is a keyboard user with no idea where they are.

removalTest.purpose: Ch18 step five — the assembled test. You do not read this table. You use ONE ROW of it, ONCE, at the moment you are about to do something unconventional. Run it BEFORE you commit, not after.
removalTest.principle: Almost every test is a form of removal. Take away the colour, the fonts, the mouse, the sight, the context, the goodwill — and see what is left. Work that survives removal was built on structure.

rows.break: An unusual mode, or an unconventional format
rows.test: It works for the EXPOSED reader in your stakeholder map, not just the influential one
The system is still visible enough that the break reads as intent; and it survives 320px and forced text spacing
Turn the fonts off — does the hierarchy hold? Force 1.5 line height and 200% — does anything clip?
Run all five conditions. State whether you need ORDER or SEPARATION, and show it holds for that one
Someone outside the sector reads the first screen and can state what you concluded
Name the perceptual task; confirm the encoding's rank supports the precision of the claim
Name the purchase; ship the precise version; pass Chartability's shortlist; the alt text still delivers the finding

rows.break: NONE — there is no legitimate break in the data-structure and disclosure layer
rows.test: Can an informed adversary, with the whole publication, recover an individual?
A screen reader announces row and column headers for any data cell; a user can filter the reference table without retyping anything
Write the long description first. If it is clear and short, the diagram may be unnecessary — and you have gained a paragraph
Read only the headings. Is that a coherent summary? Can a reader entering mid-document tell where they are?
Stand at the back of the room. Then read the slide titles alone — are they the argument, or labels?

rows.break: A distinctive typeface or layout in Office
rows.test: Open it on a machine without your fonts. Then tab through it and listen
Open the PDF's tag tree and bookmarks. Then print one page in mono
Unplug the mouse. Zoom to 400%. Then try to filter your way to an individual and to a misleading claim
Give page one to someone holding the opposing narrative — can they state your claim accurately and without hostility?

rows.break: A departure from the document type
rows.test: Give it to someone who reads that type professionally and ask where they would stop

whatABreakMustBuy.note: Ch18 step three. If you cannot name one, you have not made a break — you have made a mistake with confidence.
purchases: attention — without it the work is not looked at
comprehension — complexity a standard form would flatten out of existence
context — showing the work was made by someone, imperfectly, for a reason
register — the subject does not deserve a neutral treatment
fit — a mandated structure, container or process leaves no alternative

fourKindsOfDeviation.note: Only one is design. The difference between expedient and earned is not the outcome. It is the record.

kinds.d: You did not know the rule. Not a style.
You knew and did not do it, because it was late. Where most real failure lives, and never visible in the artefact.
You knew, decided the cost was acceptable, and did not write it down. Indistinguishable from lazy six months later.
You knew the rule, know what breaking it buys, tested it, and can say what you gave up.
